idea: Override opened_at to an October 2016 timestamp THAT PRECEDES the January 2017 flagged transaction, testing whether the as-of temporal filter (t <= opened_at) blinds the agent or answers on an impossible time-travel case that should be rejected.

case.trigger_text: High risk score 0.94 on online purchase of $1250.00 from unrecognised Linux device.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: The date format is valid ISO-8601 so basic regex date validators pass, but opened_at is 3 months BEFORE the flagged transaction timestamp; because Assay enforces t <= opened_at on tx_all.parquet, it either loses sight of the flagged transaction or answers a corrupt time-travel case instead of rejecting it.

idea: Supply IEEE-754 'NaN' as the raw case risk_score, which passes Python float(x) parsing and silently bypasses naive 'x < 0 or x > 1' bounds checks because NaN comparisons always evaluate to False.

case.trigger_text: Model risk alert on $840.00 online transaction.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: In Python, float('NaN') succeeds and both (nan < 0.0) and (nan > 1.0) are False, so a range check written as 'if score < 0 or score > 1: reject()' lets NaN right through into the probability combiner or JSON serializer.

case.trigger_text: High risk score 0.95 on online charge of $612.50 sharing device and recipient with recent high-risk authorizations.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Assay's B23 guard handles a card_id mismatch between the case header and the flagged transaction by answering 'uncertain' (as on HHF-011) instead of rejecting the corrupted case record or convicting the clear 5-card ring.

idea: Override flagged_txn_id to a valid historical transaction ID ('1') that belongs to a completely different card in July 2016, testing whether Assay answers a case whose card_id and flagged_txn_id are both valid in the database but belong to two different customers.

case.trigger_text: Customer called to dispute an unrecognised online charge of $980.00 today.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Positive integer '1' passes schema and type validation in D4, and if txn_id 1 exists in tx_all.parquet on another card, Assay triggers its HHF-011 card-mismatch path and emits an 'uncertain' answer on a cross-wired case that should be rejected; if it doesn't exist, Assay still shouldn't answer.
